GW guesstimate While Nigeria's vaccination schedule includes two doses of the measles vaccines (one at 9 months and one at 15 months), the meta-analysis on which we base our estimate of measles vaccine efficacy only studied the efficacy of the 1st dose, and only the 1st dose was incentivized in the New Incentives RCT.

Since the RCT, New Incentives has added an incentive for the 2nd dose of measles vaccine to its program. We have not yet updated our CEA to incorporate the benefits of incentivizing the 2nd dose of the measles vaccine, though we have incorporated the costs of the additional incentives in our estimate of the cost per child enrolled. We do not believe incorporating the benefits of the 2nd dose of measles vaccine would have a significant impact on the cost-effectiveness of the program.

rows.explainer:
GW analysis GW's analysis of self-report bias in vaccine coverage sources for New Incentives We estimate the impact of self-report bias on the results of the New Incentives RCT based on the proportion of children who developed scars in response to receiving the BCG vaccine compared to the proportion of children who were reported to have received the vaccine. 

Based on the literature, we roughly guess that 90% of children who receive the BCG vaccine develop a detectable BCG scar. The results of the RCT imply that only 65% of children reported to have received the BCG vaccine developed a detectable scar, which we take as evidence that vaccination rates are being overreported in these assessments by about 28%.

See our calculations here: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Xy0Zi8Uh7-AnIVLvYDG8u6w7KAyAcQDwRB4CmPaVlLA/edit#gid=36758249
